note: Hand-curated, sourced entries. Both primaries are Aug 18; frontrunners curated, not marked nominees.

FL-senate.statusNote: Special election for the seat Marco Rubio vacated. Appointed Sen. Ashley Moody (R) and state Rep. Angie Nixon (D) won their Aug 18 primaries. Nixon defeated Alex Vindman for the Democratic nomination.

FL-governor.statusNote: Open seat, Gov. DeSantis is term-limited. Rep. Byron Donalds (R) and former Rep. David Jolly (D) won their Aug 18 primaries.

candidates.name: Ashley Moody
candidates.background: Appointed to Marco Rubio's Senate seat in January 2025. Florida Attorney General 2019-2025; before that a circuit judge and federal prosecutor. Endorsed by President Trump for the special election.
priorities: Law and order; back law enforcement

cost.label: Blames inflation on the Fed and federal spending: 'We must audit the Fed!' (Fox News)

health.label: Kept Florida in suits challenging the ACA's constitutionality as AG; voted against extending ACA premium subsidies in Dec 2025 (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: 'Strengthens the border, builds the wall, and removes those who entered unlawfully' (Fox News)

safety.label: 'America First policies that promote law and order'; endorsed by the Florida Police Chiefs Association (campaign site)

repro.label: As AG, petitioned the Florida Supreme Court to disqualify the Amendment 4 abortion-rights ballot measure (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Joined Texas v. Pennsylvania seeking to invalidate 2020 results in four states; opposed felon voting-rights restoration without payment of court fees (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: Voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill extending the 2017 tax cuts, calling it 'the LARGEST tax cut for the working and middle class in history' (Senate office)

education.label: Secured a federal tax credit scholarship program so 'as many as two million students' can 'access a school or education service of their parents' choice' (Senate office)

climate.label: 0% LCV score in 2025: voted to terminate wind and solar credits, roll back the methane fee, and block state clean-car standards (League of Conservation Voters)

housing.label: Voted yes on the 89-10 ROAD to Housing Act package pairing permitting streamlining and local zoning-reform incentives with expanded CDBG and HOME affordable-construction grants (Senate roll call 53)

controversies.label: Joined the Texas v. Pennsylvania suit to invalidate 2020 results; board member of the Rule of Law Defense Fund, which promoted the pre-Jan. 6 rally (Wikipedia)

candidates.name: Alex Vindman
candidates.home: Florida (born Kyiv, came to the U.S. as a child refugee)
candidates.now: Retired Army Lt. Colonel; senior fellow, Johns Hopkins SAIS
candidates.background: Retired Army lieutenant colonel with a 21-year career including Iraq combat; National Security Council director for European affairs 2018-2020 and a key witness in the first Trump impeachment. Leads the Democratic primary field on fundraising against state Rep. Angie Nixon.
priorities: Lower costs: insurance, housing, health care

cost.label: Cut everyday costs, middle-class tax relief, crack down on corporate price gouging (campaign agenda)

health.label: Defend and strengthen the ACA, lower drug prices, add dental and vision to Medicare (campaign agenda)

housing.label: Mixed: cut construction red tape AND curb corporate investor speculation; fix the insurance crisis (campaign agenda)

immigration.label: Calls current policy 'cruel'; supports tech-driven border security plus a 'reasonable path to legal status' (candidate profile)

taxes.label: Middle-class tax cuts; close corporate loopholes (candidate profile)

climate.label: 'All-of-the-above' energy: solar, wind, nuclear, and domestic oil and gas; market-driven production (candidate profile)

education.label: Invest in teachers and public schools; opposes defunding public schools or dismantling the Dept. of Education (campaign agenda)

repro.label: 'I'll fight to restore her rights, and the rights of women across our state' (candidate profile)

democracy.label: Ban congressional stock trading with jail for violations, repeal Citizens United, refuse corporate PAC money (campaign agenda)

nullNotes.safety: checked Florida First agenda page and Smarter.vote issue profile; nothing documented beyond gun policy, which does not map to this axis; roll-call/record search also empty

sources.label: CBS News: Moody and Nixon win Aug 18 Florida Senate special primaries

candidates.name: Byron Donalds
candidates.background: U.S. Representative for southwest Florida since 2021; before Congress, a finance and banking career and two terms in the Florida House, where he shepherded the bill creating the precursor to Florida's universal school-voucher program. Brooklyn-born, raised by a single mother. Endorsed by President Trump ('RUN, BYRON, RUN!').
priorities: Implement the Trump agenda in Florida

cost.label: Affordability through deregulation: says cutting regulatory 'red tape' is crucial to lowering the cost of new homes, backs property-tax elimination (News4Jax interview)

health.label: Opposes the ACA ('a ruse... to seize control'); favors cross-state insurance sales and tax incentives (House issues page)

housing.label: Cut regulatory red tape to lower the cost of new homes and apartments (News4Jax interview)

immigration.label: 'Secure the border, keep our families and communities safe, end taxpayer handouts to illegals' (campaign site)

taxes.label: Supports DeSantis's push to eliminate property taxes for homesteaded residents; less regulation to cut costs (News4Jax interview)

education.label: School-choice champion: shepherded the bill creating the precursor to Florida's universal voucher program; 'I've been in this fight my whole career' (WUSF)

safety.label: 'Backing our law enforcement, enforcing the law'; keep Florida a 'law-and-order state' (Florida's Voice roundtable)

repro.label: Publicly opposed Amendment 4, the 2024 abortion-rights ballot measure, urging Floridians to vote no (Florida's Voice)

democracy.label: Voted to object to certifying Arizona and Pennsylvania 2020 electors; said in 2023 Biden was 'not the legitimate president' (Wikipedia)

controversies.label: June 2024 remarks that Black families were 'together' under Jim Crow drew wide criticism; 2024 Campaign Legal Center complaint over ~$1.6M in undisclosed stock trades (Wikipedia)

candidates.name: David Jolly
candidates.background: Fifth-generation Floridian and former Republican congressman (2014-2017) who left the GOP in 2018 and registered as a Democrat in 2025. Attorney and former MSNBC political analyst. Leads the Democratic primary field in polling.
priorities: Fix the property-insurance crisis with a state catastrophic fund
Invest in public schools; reform vouchers

cost.label: State catastrophic fund to pull natural-disaster risk out of the private market and 'dramatically reduce property and car insurance rates' (campaign site)

health.label: Expand Medicaid; supports the ACA; protect access despite federal cuts (campaign site)

housing.label: Insurance fix plus no-interest condo-repair loans; 'reducing costs for homeowners, renters, and retirees' (campaign site)

immigration.label: 'Florida should embrace our immigrant community and celebrate their contributions' (campaign site)

climate.label: Accepts climate science; resilience investment; require more clean energy in public utilities (campaign site)

education.label: Dramatically increase public-school investment and teacher pay; means-test and cap vouchers (campaign site)

safety.label: Mixed: hold lawbreakers accountable while correcting racial disparities; local control of community policing (campaign site)

repro.label: 'Decisions... between women and their doctors, not politicians'; codify the Roe/Casey framework (campaign site)

democracy.label: Oppose legislative preemption of voter initiatives; enforce constitutional amendments passed at 50%+ (campaign site)

taxes.label: One of only three House Republicans to vote no on the 2015 Death Tax Repeal Act, a $269 billion estate tax cut that passed 240-179 (The Hill, House Clerk roll call 161)

controversies.label: Attacked by primary rivals over his past GOP 'life begins at conception' record; says his position evolved (CBS Miami)
